checked_claim: Review prophylaxis versus treatment, formulation, the current kidney-function estimate and units required by the product guidance, and any dialysis. The consensus renal-dose table uses Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance in mL/min, which is not the same quantity as indexed eGFR in mL/min/1.73 m². A renal-adjusted dose may need to change as graft function changes. Routine mini-dosing below the appropriate renal dose is not recommended. This case supplies no complete dosing calculation; use the actual product guidance with transplant/pharmacy review. In a D+/R− kidney recipient intolerant of valganciclovir or ganciclovir prophylaxis, the consensus suggests switching to a deliverable preemptive strategy or letermovir prophylaxis; the recommendation is weak with low-quality evidence. Do not replace a full review with an arbitrary low valganciclovir dose. The adult EU kidney-transplant letermovir indication is CMV prophylaxis in D+/R− recipients weighing at least 40 kg. The transplant team must check current product information and the individual situation; this is not permission to apply the same indication to all R+ recipients. For this EU kidney-transplant indication, letermovir starts on the transplant day or by day 7 and continues through day 200. A later switch discussed in the consensus needs a separate specialist and regulatory assessment; do not silently treat it as the same labelled start schedule. Letermovir can increase tacrolimus exposure. Arrange frequent whole-blood tacrolimus concentration measurements during coadministration and at letermovir discontinuation, with specialist dose adjustment. A universal percentage reduction is not a substitute for measured exposure. The SmPC calls for increased monitoring during the first two weeks after starting and stopping; route changes also require monitoring. Ciclosporin has a bidirectional interaction with letermovir: review the required letermovir dose adjustment and monitor ciclosporin concentrations. Kidney-function measurements alone do not replace immunosuppressant-level monitoring. Letermovir does not protect against herpes simplex or varicella-zoster. Review separate prophylaxis when indicated. CMV prophylaxis evidence does not establish treatment of breakthrough CMV disease. Routine DNA monitoring is not recommended while appropriate prophylaxis is being taken reliably. New absorption or adherence concerns, changing kidney function or augmented immunosuppression can justify testing for breakthrough DNAemia and clinical reassessment. Debrief: write down the current indication, renal-dose review process, interaction monitoring at letermovir initiation and discontinuation, other herpesvirus prevention if indicated, and the named team to contact for new symptoms. Do not wait for a routine sample to seek assessment of persistent vomiting.

teaching_claims.authored_claim: Letermovir can increase tacrolimus exposure. Arrange frequent whole-blood tacrolimus concentration measurements during coadministration and at letermovir discontinuation, with specialist dose adjustment. A universal percentage reduction is not a substitute for measured exposure. The SmPC calls for increased monitoring during the first two weeks after starting and stopping; route changes also require monitoring.
